artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p>3$ be a prime. Prove or disprove the following statements.

(1) If $p\equiv 1\pmod 6$ and $p=x^2+3y^2$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv 4x^2-2p\pmod{p^2}\quad\text{and}\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv \frac{p-4x^2}{3}\pmod{p^2}.$$

(2) If $p\equiv 5\pmod 6$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv 0\pmod{p^2}\quad\text{and}\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv \frac{p}{3}\pmod{p^2}.$$

(3) For every positive integer $a$,
$$p^a\sum_{k=0}^{p^a-1}\frac{(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv 1+\frac{7}{6}p^3 B_{p-3}\pmod{p^4},$$
where $B_n$ denotes the $n$th Bernoulli number.

(4) One has
$$\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv p+2\Big(\frac{-1}{p}\Big)p^3 E_{p-3}\pmod{p^4},$$
where $E_n$ denotes the $n$th Euler number and $\big(\frac{\cdot}{p}\big)$ is the Legendre symbol.

(5) For every integer $n\geq 2$,
$$\frac{2n}{\binom{2n}{n}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^{n-1-k}}\in\mathbb{Z}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Several parts of this multi-part conjecture have been addressed in the literature. The Dwork-type supercongruence in part (3) (the $p^a$ statement) is related to work of Guo–Zudilin and a proof by Y. Zhang and P. Yuan establishing $\sum_{k=0}^{p^r-1}(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3/16^k\equiv p\sum_{k=0}^{p^{r-1}-1}(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3/16^k\pmod{p^{3r+1-\delta_{p,3}}}$, and Beukers' method has been applied to similar families. However, no single reference verified in the search establishes the full set of statements (the precise mod $p^2$ identities for the unweighted sums in terms of $p=x^2+3y^2$, the mod $p^4$ refinement involving $B_{p-3}$ and $E_{p-3}$, and the integrality assertion), so the conjecture as a whole appears only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Proof of a Dwork-type supercongruence by induction
status_evidence.snippet: For any prime p≥3 and integer r≥1, the sum of (3k+1)/16^k * binomial(2k,k)^3 from k=0 to p^r-1 is congruent to p times the analogous sum from k=0 to p^(r-1)-1 modulo p^(3r+1-δ_{p,3}).
status_evidence.claim: A Dwork-type version of part (3) has been proved, extending Guo–Zudilin.

status_evidence.title: Supercongruences via Beukers' method
status_evidence.snippet: Beukers has developed a unified method using modular forms that can deal with a large number of supercongruences involving binomial coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: General methods exist that handle many such supercongruences, but the full conjecture A6 is not stated as fully proved.

status_evidence.title: On a supercongruence conjecture of Z.-W. Sun
status_evidence.snippet: We partly prove a supercongruence conjectured by Z.-W. Sun in 2013.
status_evidence.claim: Related Sun conjectures on sums involving binom(2k,k)/16^k have been only partly proved.
